config.title: Christmas Markets Near Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Christmas market day trips from Berlin for Advent 2026, checked against the organisers' own pages and the train timetable on 23 October.

items.q: What is the best Christmas market day trip from Berlin?
items.a: For one free day, **Leipzig**: the direct ICE takes about 1 hour 15 minutes and the market fills the old town from **24 November to 23 December**. For a short half day, **Potsdam**, under an hour away. Dresden's Striezelmarkt is the most famous, but two hours each way leaves you about eight hours at the stalls.

items.q: Can I do the Dresden Striezelmarkt as a day trip from Berlin?
items.a: Yes. Direct trains take a little over two hours. Leave Berlin around 10:00 and you are at the Altmarkt by about 12:30. On Saturday 5 December the **last direct train back leaves Dresden at 20:53**; after that the way home takes until past midnight.

items.q: When do the Christmas markets near Berlin open in 2026?
items.a: Potsdam's Weihnachtszauber and Cottbus open on **23 November**, Leipzig on **24 November** and Dresden's Striezelmarkt on **25 November**. The weekend markets start on the first Advent weekend: Babelsberg from **27 November**, Lübbenau and Quedlinburg from **28 November**.

items.q: Do I need tickets for the Spreewald Christmas market?
items.a: The harbour market in Lübbenau is free, but the **punt ride and the Lehde open-air museum need a timed ticket**. Sales started on 1 September and unsold places are released on **1 November**. The Spreewaldweihnacht runs only on **28-29 November and 5-6 December**.

items.q: Which Christmas markets near Berlin can I reach with the Deutschlandticket?
items.a: **Potsdam, Lübbenau and Cottbus** are on regional trains, so the Deutschlandticket covers them. Leipzig, Dresden and Quedlinburg are only realistic on long-distance trains; the regional routes take about three to four hours each way.

items.q: Is Quedlinburg worth the trip from Berlin at Christmas?
items.a: If you love old towns, yes, but plan it. It takes close to **three hours** (2:45 on the fastest trains) with a change in Magdeburg, and **Advent in the Courtyards** opens only on **28-29 November, 5-6 and 12-13 December**, 11:00 to 19:00. That gives you about six hours there.
